name: Alien Egg
summary: Wind serpents guard an unfamiliar clutch in Thousand Needles, and tauren scouts at Freewind Post want to know why.

sections.title: A Serpent's Brood
sections.body: Alien Egg lies at the base of spires south and northeast of Freewind Post. Native wind serpents guard it beside their own nests, though such a clutch is strange among the life on the canyon floor. Hagar Lightninghoof, a tauren brave watching from Freewind Post, wants to retrieve it. He hopes to learn whether it threatens the mesa settlements or is simply an unusual local reptile.

sections.title: The Spawn of Arikara
sections.body: At Freewind Post, Alien Egg opens under closer inspection. Arikara, the red wind serpent of tauren legend, emerges from the shell. The tauren believe Arikara is a spirit of vengeance. The young serpent takes flight, and a shaken Hagar declares that vengeance has come to Thousand Needles. Local defenders set out to confront her.

faq.answer: The tauren scouts call Alien Egg alien because it is completely foreign and unfamiliar to them. Its colors and markings differ from ordinary wind serpent clutches in Thousand Needles.

faq.q: Where can the Alien Egg be found?
faq.answer: Alien Egg lies on the canyon floor near mesa walls south and northeast of Freewind Post in Thousand Needles. Hostile wind serpents surround and guard it.

faq.q: Why do the local serpents guard the egg?
faq.answer: No one knows why the local serpents guard Alien Egg. They protect it as if it were their own, and those who have seen it have not come close enough to examine it.

faq.q: What happens when you bring the egg to Hagar Lightninghoof?
faq.answer: When you bring Alien Egg to Hagar Lightninghoof at Freewind Post, it hatches before his eyes. What emerges shakes Hagar so badly that he immediately seeks counsel from Motega Firemane.

angles.text: As a tauren, you keep watch over the canyon from Freewind Post. Unknown creatures can seem like an omen or a direct threat to your precarious cliffside home.
As a hunter, you know wind serpents are among the most revered beasts of the Kalimdor barrens. Tracking one of their rarest and most guarded clutches tests your instincts.
